description: The prepaid balance alert settings card is absent, without residual layout, while release-v1.5-feature is loading, unavailable, or disabled.
The dedicated settings read and update actions independently fail closed behind release-v1.5-feature and retain billing_settings.read and billing_settings.update permissions.
The scan subscriber performs no evaluation, alert, delivery, or notification write when release-v1.5-feature is disabled or its checker is unavailable.
An authorized MSP user sees a Prepaid balance alerts card after Credit Expiration Settings and before External Credit Settings on a client's Billing > General tab.
The settings card independently configures a positive minor-unit credit threshold with ISO currency and an integer bucket threshold from 1 through 100 percent.

The settings card defaults a new credit policy to the client's default currency, offers client-recipient opt-in only when an alert type is enabled, and explains that checks run daily at 09:00 UTC without an immediate send.
The dedicated settings update validates paired credit amount and uppercase ISO currency, valid threshold ranges, tenant/client scope, and forces client opt-in off when both alert types are disabled.
The settings update partially upserts only the four new alert-policy columns and never invokes broad null-delete billing-settings behavior.
The migration adds nullable credit amount/currency and bucket-percent settings plus a false-by-default client opt-in with database range and pairing constraints.
The migration creates tenant-distributed prepaid_balance_alerts with composite tenant keys, a tenant-unique dedupe key, lifecycle snapshots, payload, resolution fields, and scan indexes.

The migration creates tenant-distributed prepaid_balance_alert_deliveries with unique per-alert channel/recipient identity, role metadata, attempts, leases, errors, terminal timestamps, and a claim index.
Both new tenant tables are registered in runtime and migration tenant metadata, and the down migration drops deliveries before alerts before removing settings columns and checks.
Credit evaluation sums only non-expired credit_tracking.remaining_amount for the configured client and currency using canonical credit-balance semantics.
Credit evaluation skips a configured client/currency with no credit history but treats a historically funded zero balance as eligible.
Credit opens one alert only when available value is strictly below the threshold, deduplicates while low, and resolves/rearms at equality or above.
prdRefs: Users and Primary Flows > Daily scan identifies low prepaid credit

description: Changing the credit amount or currency resolves the prior episode with policy_changed and evaluates the replacement policy as a new episode.
Bucket evaluation resolves current client-owned Bucket configurations through client_contracts, contracts, contract_lines, and contract_line_service_configuration without using client_contract_lines.
Each current bucket period evaluates minutes_used against total_minutes plus rolled_over_minutes using exact cross-multiplication, inclusive threshold equality, and unclamped overage.
prdRefs: Users and Primary Flows > Daily scan identifies a consumed bucket

description: A non-positive bucket capacity is skipped with a structured warning and cannot open an alert.
A bucket alert is sent once per bucket_usage period and configured percentage; a new period is eligible and a percentage change closes and re-evaluates the prior policy alert.
Per-client evaluation locks client_billing_settings in a short transaction, while tenant-unique alert and delivery constraints make replayed or concurrent scans harmless.
An active assigned account manager receives a preference-aware high-priority internal warning and, when valid, email; missing or inactive managers do not abort the scan.
Client email is planned only after per-client opt-in and resolves exactly one canonical invoice billing recipient with recipientClientId locale behavior.
Manager and client addresses are trim/lowercase normalized, collapse to one email delivery when equal, and retain both roles in delivery metadata.
Enabling client opt-in during an open alert may add its absent delivery, while manager reassignment or recipient changes never resend a role that already succeeded for that alert.
Credit-low and bucket-threshold email/internal subtypes and complete localized templates are registered with warning internal type, high default priority, required values, and role-safe links.
All settings copy is added to every msp/clients locale including pseudo-locales, without adding a new preference screen.
CE schedules the separate prepaid-balance-alert-scan job per tenant at 0 9 * * * through the existing singleton scheduled-job path.
EE reuses the global maintenance fanout to invoke prepaid-balance-alert-scan at 09:00 UTC with overlap policy SKIP and the existing short catch-up convention.
The server-free jobs handler rejects missing tenant context and publishes PREPAID_BALANCE_ALERT_SCAN_REQUESTED without importing server billing, PostHog, or notification code.
The server subscriber owns flag evaluation, canonical ledger queries, client locking, alert lifecycle, recipient planning, delivery claims, and per-tenant error isolation.
Pending and retryable deliveries are claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, worker leases, stale-lease reclamation, and a maximum of five attempts.
Internal notification creation and delivery success are committed together through createNotificationFromTemplateInternal(trx, ...), making replay transactionally idempotent.
Email sends outside the claim transaction, records success afterward, retries transient failures within the five-attempt bound, and documents the provider-acceptance crash window as at-least-once.
Preference-disabled deliveries are terminal skipped records, while missing or invalid recipients remain auditable and may be resolved on a later scan when no successful role delivery exists.
Every tenant scan emits a structured summary of evaluated subjects, lifecycle decisions, delivery outcomes, retries, exhaustion, and invalid subjects.
Structured warnings identify actionable tenant/client/alert/delivery/bucket/currency context without logging raw recipient addresses or template bodies.
Disabling release-v1.5-feature after rollout makes scheduling effects inert without deleting nullable policy settings, alert history, or delivery audit rows.
